adderboard.method: Seeks the smallest autoregressive Transformer for ten-digit addition, with separate trained and analytically specified weight tracks. Coding agents contributed to some analytic constructions.
adderboard.relation: An example of tiny-network construction explicitly mentioned in the WSP report. The analytic track is the closest comparison; the whole single-task leaderboard should not be treated as a gradient-free method or general weight programming.

fast.method: One network produces context-dependent weight updates that control another network's fast memory. The system is trained using gradients.
fast.relation: Historical background: one network programming another predates WSP. This differs from a general-purpose LLM editing weights to meet a natural-language goal.

es.method: Uses parameter perturbations and rewards to estimate update directions and train policies through black-box optimization, without backpropagating through the target network.
es.relation: Optimization background: avoiding target-network backpropagation is not new. ES relies on randomized search and feedback rather than an LLM's mechanistic reasoning to choose edits.

rewrite.method: Treats a layer of a generative model as a linear associative memory and locally rewrites the generative rules encoded in it.
rewrite.relation: Editing background: changes rules inside a model rather than just its outputs. Researchers design the editing algorithm instead of a general-purpose LLM devising it autonomously.

rasp.method: Introduces RASP, expressing programs such as counting and sorting through abstractions of attention and feedforward computation.
rasp.relation: Construction background: expresses algorithms as computations a Transformer can implement. RASP itself is not a compiler that directly outputs weights.

soups.method: Averages the weights of multiple models fine-tuned from the same pretrained model, combining them into one model.
soups.relation: Weight-arithmetic background: combines already trained weights. The capabilities come from fine-tuning results, rather than modifications constructed through LLM reasoning.

actadd.method: Constructs a behavioral direction from differences in intermediate activations on contrasting prompts, then adds it during forward passes.
actadd.relation: A nearby directional intervention: controls runtime activations without permanently writing the intervention into weights. This should be distinguished from weight orthogonalization.

repe.method: Reads and intervenes on internal representations of high-level behavior, analyzing population-level representations rather than individual neurons.
repe.relation: Related representation analysis and control: helps explain where behavioral directions come from, but is not the same as a general-purpose LLM autonomously reading and writing weights.

thinkedit.method: Extracts a direction from long and short reasoning activations, locates short-reasoning attention heads, and orthogonalizes their output weights without a gradient optimizer for the edit.
thinkedit.relation: A close methodological comparison for WSP's Qwen experiment: both repair reasoning through local weight interventions. ThinkEdit addresses overly short reasoning; WSP addresses repetitive loops, with an LLM organizing diagnosis and editing.

weightsteer.method: Fine-tunes opposite behaviors separately, subtracts the two weight updates to obtain a direction, and adds or removes it to steer behavior.
weightsteer.relation: Related weight-direction editing: connects task vectors with behavioral steering. Its direction comes from two fine-tunes, so the full procedure is not training-free.

d2l.method: A specially trained hypernetwork converts document context into a LoRA adapter in one forward pass, enabling subsequent questions without rereading the original context.
d2l.relation: Related weight generation: external information enters parameters directly. It relies on a trained amortized generator rather than a general-purpose LLM autonomously analyzing weights.

l2w.method: Uses Jacobian lens to locate components associated with a semantic target, then performs local post-editing through counterexample-guided closing and reopening of components.
l2w.relation: A related goal-driven editing workflow: localization, intervention, and validation form a loop. Localization uses Jacobians, so the entire pipeline should not be labeled gradient-free.

learnopt.method: Trains an LSTM to learn parameter-update rules, making the optimizer itself learnable.
learnopt.relation: A network deciding how another network updates already has precedents. Specialized training and gradients distinguish it from reasoning-driven editing by a general-purpose LLM.

hyper.method: Trains one network to generate another network's weights.
hyper.relation: Network-generated weights predate WSP. WSP investigates the weight-reading and writing capabilities already available in a general-purpose LLM.

mend.method: Trains an auxiliary editing network to transform the target model's gradients into fast local updates.
mend.relation: A model editing another model is not new. MEND uses a specially trained editor and target-model gradients during editing.

circuits.method: Explains computational circuits in small Transformers using the residual stream and compositions of QK and OV matrices.
circuits.relation: Provides a framework for inferring computation from weights. WSP explores whether an LLM can perform related analyses autonomously.

rome.method: Locates factual recall through causal interventions, then applies a rank-one edit to MLP weights.
rome.relation: Mechanism localization followed by local weight editing has precedents. ROME uses a dedicated algorithm, while WSP puts an LLM in charge of designing the approach.

task.method: Subtracts original weights from fine-tuned weights to obtain task vectors, then adds, subtracts, scales, or combines them.
task.relation: Weight-direction editing predates WSP. Task vectors come from fine-tuning; WSP's modifications come from operations designed by the LLM.

tracr.method: Compiles formal RASP programs into Transformer weights that implement computations such as counting and sorting.
tracr.relation: Constructing weights without training the target network has precedents. WSP explores whether an LLM can design computations from task descriptions and write them into weights.

nfn.method: Designs networks that respect neuron-permutation symmetries to process other networks' weights or gradients.
nfn.relation: Models that analyze or transform weights as data already exist. These use specialized architectures and training.

openai.method: GPT-4 proposes neuron explanations from text and activation samples, then tests them through activation prediction.
openai.relation: General-purpose LLMs explaining models predate WSP. The core evidence is activation samples and the main output is an explanation, rather than a weight edit.

opro.method: An LLM proposes new candidates using an objective, previous candidates, and scores, iteratively optimizing mainly prompts.
opro.relation: The propose–evaluate–revise outer loop has precedents. WSP extends the objects being manipulated to weights and weight-editing programs.

caa.method: Extracts a direction from activation differences between positive and negative behavioral examples, adding or subtracting it during inference to adjust behavior.
caa.relation: Behavioral direction control has precedents. CAA changes runtime activations; WSP's writing experiments modify stored weights.

patch.method: Patches hidden representations into another model computation and uses the generated language to explain them.
patch.relation: Model-assisted interpretation of internal information has precedents. The main objects are hidden representations, rather than weights themselves.

maia.method: A vision-language model calls tools, proposes hypotheses, and iterates on experiments to explain features and discover failure modes.
maia.relation: Autonomous agents analyzing models predate WSP. The analysis workflow is related, but programming target weights is not the core objective.

direction.method: Extracts a behavioral direction, applies directional ablation, and makes the intervention persistent through weight orthogonalization.
direction.relation: A close operational comparison for WSP's Qwen direction edit. WSP puts the LLM in charge of diagnosis, localization, and intervention selection.

t2l.method: A specially trained hypernetwork generates a LoRA adapter in one forward pass from a natural-language task description.
t2l.relation: Natural language to weight updates has precedents. It relies on a specially trained generator, unlike a general-purpose LLM autonomously analyzing and designing edits.

wsp.method: A general-purpose LLM reads, repairs, or constructs network weights around natural-language goals. Some experiments use forward-pass feedback.
wsp.relation: Assigns analysis, editing, and construction to a general-purpose LLM. Target-weight edits do not use a gradient optimizer; this does not imply no examples, feedback, or experimental selection.
